exercises.title: Irreducibility of $x^3-2$
exercises.description:
Consider $f(x)=x^3-2$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ and $\mathbb{R}$.

a) Show irreducibility over $\mathbb{Q}$.
b) Factorize $f$ over $\mathbb{R}$.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Rational root test
Possible rational roots are $\pm1, \pm2$.
None are roots, so $f$ is irreducible over $\mathbb{Q}$.

Step 2: Real factorization
There is a real root $\sqrt[3]{2}$.
Thus $f(x)=(x-\sqrt[3]{2})(x^2+\sqrt[3]{2}x+\sqrt[3]{4})$ over $\mathbb{R}$

b) Find eigenvectors.

exercises.title: Basis of a Span
exercises.description:
Given $v_1=(1,0,1)$, $v_2=(2,1,3)$, $v_3=(3,1,4)$.

a) Test linear independence.
b) Find a basis of the span.
c) Express $v_3$ in the basis.
solutionSteps:
Step 2: Independence
Thus $v_1,v_2$ are independent, $v_3$ is dependent.

Step 3: Basis and representation
Basis: $\{v_1,v_2\}$
$v_3 = 1\cdot v_1 + 1\cdot v_2$

exercises.title: Solving a Congruence
exercises.description:
Solve the congruence $7x \equiv 5 \pmod{26}$.
Also determine the multiplicative inverse of 7 modulo 26.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Find the inverse
Find $a$ with $7a\equiv1\pmod{26}$.
$7\cdot15=105\equiv1\pmod{26}$, so $7^{-1}\equiv15$
